description: Option E (qou-99qc) reframed as a level test: on the H_3(q) normal-form basis tr_M^z is quadratic in z, so a candidate Delta DETERMINES the functional it would need, and that functional is a Wenzl level. Solves the required level for every candidate in the corpus's own Delta census plus all 16 readings of the properties blocks' recipe. None requires an admissible level (r = 1 augmentation, r = 2 convention D). Selects nothing; scope-(a).

data.markov_convention: both admissible parameters are evaluated: z = q (level 1, the augmentation) and z_D = q^3/(q^2+1) (level 2, convention D)

caveats: Scope-(a). It measures the candidates the corpus has ALREADY built; it does not show that no element can require an admissible level, and Option E stays open.

Deliberately NOT a search. Enumerating elements until one lands on r = 1 or r = 2 would be selection against the target — a fit under AGENTS.md 'NO FITTING'. The 16-variant family is reported as a range for exactly that reason; its best-landing member is not a result.

The level ladder z(r) is the n = 3 Wenzl relation Q^r = z_W/(1 - Q + z_W) with Q = q^2, z_W = q z; admissibility as 'r in {1,2}' is the n = 3 statement, checked at n = 3..7 in qbeta_wenzl_level_decides_the_functional_probe but not proved for all n.
The candidate constructors are IMPORTED from qbeta_delta_candidate_census_probe, so any defect in those models propagates here unchanged. This probe adds no model of its own.

Q_beta is the AME-2020 value; the CODATA-2022-derived one differs by +191 ppb (bean qou-0e2p). At the residual scale seen here (tens of percent) that choice is immaterial, and it is NOT immaterial for any claim at the sigma = 779.7 ppb level.
